problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2y+z)?$
worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2y+z) & =c \\ x-2y+z & ={e}^{c}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the exponent ${e}^{c}$ is positive for all $-\infty <c<\infty .$ If we let ${e}^{c}={r}^{2},$ we get a family of planes:

$$
x-2y+z={r}^{2},\,r\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
